title: Omega(n^(2/3)m^(1/3)) sample lower bound for equivalence testing of distribution collections under uniform sampling
author: Reut Levi, Dana Ron, and Ronitt Rubinfeld
work: Testing Properties of Collections of Distributions
source_version: Theory of Computing volume 9 article 8 (2013), official complete journal PDF acquired 2026-09-30; canonical DOI 10.4086/toc.2013.v009a008 verified against official landing and printed PDF header
difficulty_reason: After named Poissonization, fingerprint symmetry and Roos/Pinsker prerequisites, the proof still must establish the new list-distribution fingerprint indistinguishability reduction, construct a simultaneously balanced matrix controlling all row subsets, and estimate all five histogram families while separating the hard collections. These complete authored constructions and bounds occur in Section3.1–3.3, not a citation to the previous single/pair-distribution result. The m-dependent lower bound and heavy/light variance masking comprise one H2 sample-complexity task beyond ordinary two-point testing or concentration qualifications.

source_check.note: Exact original Theorem3.1 only: for every epsilon<=1/20 and n>c m log m for a sufficiently large constant c, testing equivalence of a collection of m distributions on [n] under uniform sampling requires Omega(n^{2/3}m^{1/3}) samples. Full original sampling/distance model and Section3.1–3.3 are retained, including new generalized fingerprint theorem, all authored Poisson approximation/distance proofs, balanced matrix construction, two hard collections, separation proof, every histogram-family bound and final delta=1/200 closing. Named fingerprint symmetry, Roos approximation, Chernoff/Bernoulli/Pinsker and standard Poisson facts retain exact citations/hypotheses. The author-defined conf=0 journal branch is mechanically selected with physical newline preservation; conf=1 conference alternatives stay private. Independence-testing corollary and upper-bound/testing algorithms are unselected and uncounted. All-page source/output QA completed and exact final actual logs checked. Source-material candidate only; no admission/remote-delivery credit. Root admitted this exact original authored material as one H2 unit; source quirks retained unchanged.
